title: PPF for NRIs: Continuing Your Account After Moving Abroad
description: Existing Public Provident Fund (PPF) accounts can be continued by Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) until their original maturity period. NRIs are not permitted to .

faq.q: Can an NRI open a new PPF account?
faq.a: No, NRIs are not eligible to open new PPF accounts. The scheme is exclusively for resident Indian citizens.

faq.q: Do NRIs lose tax benefits on PPF interest?
faq.a: No, the interest earned on an existing PPF account continues to be tax-exempt for NRIs, similar to resident Indians.

faq.q: What happens if I accidentally contribute to my PPF after becoming an NRI?
faq.a: Any contributions made after acquiring NRI status are treated as irregular. They may not earn interest and could be returned to you without interest.

faq.q: Can I extend my PPF account as an NRI?
faq.a: Yes, you can extend your PPF account in blocks of 5 years after maturity, but strictly without making any further contributions.

faq.q: Is premature closure allowed for NRIs?
faq.a: Yes, premature closure is allowed for NRIs after 5 financial years from the end of the year of opening, specifically on grounds of change in residency status, among others.

faq.q: What if I become a foreign citizen?
faq.a: If you acquire foreign citizenship, your PPF account must be closed immediately. Interest will be paid only up to the end of the financial year preceding the year of becoming a foreign citizen.
